body.text: How much does MuseumPass Türkiye cost in 2026?

In 2026, the official [MuseumPass Türkiye E-Kart](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-27-009) costs €165 for foreign visitors and stays valid for 15 consecutive days starting from your first turnstile scan. Regional alternatives also exist on the Ministry of Culture and Tourism portal: MuseumPass İstanbul (€105 for 5 days), MuseumPass The Aegean (€95 for 7 days), and MuseumPass Cappadocia (€65 for 3 days).

Since the Ministry pegged foreign admission fees to the euro, gate prices are charged in Turkish lira at the prevailing exchange rate on the day you buy. Each pass grants one entry per included site and is strictly non-transferable. It is also worth noting that official passes do not cover Night Museum (Gece Müzeciliği) entries after 19:00; for instance, pass holders must enter Galata Tower by 18:14 and Istanbul Archaeology Museums by 18:45, according to [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-05-009).

body.text: Which major sights (Hagia Sophia, Basilica Cistern, Dolmabahçe) are NOT included?

Three of Istanbul's highest-demand landmarks—Hagia Sophia, the Basilica Cistern, and Dolmabahçe Palace—are completely excluded from both MuseumPass Türkiye and MuseumPass İstanbul. Because different institutions manage them (the Presidency of Religious Affairs, the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality, and the Directorate of National Palaces respectively), you must buy separate tickets at their gates or official channels.
Expect to budget separately for these major exclusions in 2026:

items: Hagia Sophia (Visitor Gallery): €25 per foreign adult for upper-gallery access, as verified in [2026 Istanbul official ticket schedules](https://istanbulauthority.com/en/articles/istanbul-official-tickets). MuseumPass is not accepted.

Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı): Operated by the municipality; daytime entry runs roughly 1,950–2,250 TL (around €38–€42), rising to 3,000 TL for evening visits, per [2026 Basilica Cistern fee listings](https://www.basilicacistern.gen.tr/basilica-cistern-ticket-price/).
Dolmabahçe Palace: Managed by National Palaces (Milli Saraylar); combined entry costs roughly 2,000 TL (~€40) and requires its own ticket.

Paid Sub-Sections Inside Covered Sites: Even at included sites, the Dark Church inside Göreme Open Air Museum and the Antique Pool at [Pamukkale](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-26-009) require separate add-on tickets. Verify Topkapı Palace Harem inclusions on your exact purchase date, as combined Topkapı tickets cost 2,750 TL (~€55).

body.text: When does the pass actually save money vs single tickets?

MuseumPass Türkiye breaks even once your combined single-ticket total crosses €165 within 15 days. On a classic 10-to-14-day route hitting Istanbul, Cappadocia, Pamukkale, and Ephesus, single tickets easily reach €190 to €235, giving you €25 to €70 in real savings plus direct turnstile access without queuing at cash desks.

Run the numbers against the official [muze.gov.tr E-Ticket price sheet](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-ekle?catalogNo=WEB-PMK01-87-009) and [Pamukkale 2026 tariffs](https://clevertourists.com/resources/pamukkale-day-trip-travertines-hierapolis-tickets-guide):

items: Istanbul (covered sites): Topkapı Palace (~€55), Galata Tower (€30), Istanbul Archaeology Museums (€15), Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (€17) = €117.
Cappadocia: Göreme Open Air Museum (€20), Derinkuyu or Kaymaklı Underground City (€13), Ihlara Valley (€15) = €48.
Aegean & Pamukkale: Ephesus + Experience Museum (€40), Ephesus Terrace Houses (€15), Hierapolis & Pamukkale (€30) = €85.

body.text: That multi-region loop totals €250 in single tickets—saving €85 with the €165 national pass. By contrast, a four-day Istanbul visitor who mainly wants Hagia Sophia, Basilica Cistern, Dolmabahçe, and Topkapı will spend far less buying individual tickets. If your trip also involves [domestic flights in Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/domestic-flights-in-turkey) or [high-speed YHT trains](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/trains-in-turkey-guide), map your museum days tightly inside the 15-day clock before activating the card.
Where do you buy it without third-party markups?

Buy directly through the Ministry of Culture and Tourism's [official MuseumPass portal](https://muze.gov.tr/MuseumPass) or in person at the ticket desk of any covered state museum—such as the Istanbul Archaeology Museums or Göreme Open Air Museum—where queues are short. Third-party "city pass" websites frequently bundle commercial perks and charge 20% to 50% more than official gate rates.

Commercial cards with similar names (such as private "Istanbul Tourist Passes") are not government products. Before paying online, double-check that your browser URL reads muze.gov.tr. Buying at your first low-queue museum desk—for example, the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts on Sultanahmet Square—takes under five minutes and avoids foreign card verification glitches on the government website.

faq.q: Does MuseumPass Türkiye let you skip security lines?
faq.a: No. The pass lets you bypass the ticket-buying desk and go straight to the turnstiles, but every visitor must still clear mandatory security screening at major sites like Topkapı Palace and Ephesus.

faq.q: Can two travelers share one MuseumPass Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Each pass is strictly valid for one individual and allows only one entry per museum. Attempting to scan the same QR code or card twice at a turnstile will be blocked.

faq.q: Is Topkapı Palace Harem included in MuseumPass Türkiye in 2026?
faq.a: Coverage of Topkapı Palace's Harem and Hagia Irene has shifted in past seasons. Check the current museum list on [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/MuseumPass) right before purchasing so you know whether a courtyard add-on ticket is required.

faq.q: Do children need a MuseumPass Türkiye?
faq.a: Foreign children under 8 years old enter Ministry of Culture and Tourism museums free of charge with a valid passport showing proof of age. Children aged 8 and above pay full adult foreign-visitor rates.

faq.q: When does the 15-day MuseumPass Türkiye validity clock start?
faq.a: The 15-day countdown starts at the exact moment you scan your pass at your first museum or archaeological site, not on the date you purchase it online.

faq.q: Does MuseumPass Türkiye include public transport in Istanbul?
faq.a: No. MuseumPass covers museum and archaeological site admissions only. For ferries, trams, and metro lines in Istanbul, buy a separate Istanbulkart at any station kiosk.
